title: directed acyclic graphs and topological ordering
concepts: A directed acyclic graph (DAG) has directed edges and no directed cycle; its vertices can be ordered so every edge points forward in the order.
Topological ordering models prerequisite constraints, dependency builds, and other partial orders; independent vertices can appear in multiple valid orders.
Kahn's algorithm repeatedly removes a zero-indegree vertex and decrements its outgoing neighbors; processing fewer than V vertices proves a directed cycle exists.
DFS topological ordering appends a vertex after exploring descendants and reverses postorder; cycle detection requires distinguishing active recursion-stack nodes from fully processed nodes.
A queue gives any valid Kahn ordering, while a priority queue can select the smallest available vertex for the lexicographically smallest ordering at additional cost.
Topological order enables dynamic programming on DAGs because each predecessor can be processed before the state that depends on it.
A topological ordering exists only for a DAG; applying either algorithm to cyclic dependencies must report failure rather than present a partial list as valid.
The standard adjacency-list algorithms run in O(V+E), with indegree storage or traversal state requiring O(V) additional space.

practiceProblems.name: Course Schedule
practiceProblems.statement: Given numCourses and pairs [course, prerequisite], determine whether every course can be completed.

practiceProblems.name: Course Schedule II
practiceProblems.statement: Given numCourses and pairs [course, prerequisite], return any ordering in which every prerequisite precedes its course; return an empty array when no complete ordering exists.

practiceProblems.name: Alien Dictionary
patterns: derive precedence edges from adjacent words
practiceProblems.statement: Given words claimed to be sorted in an unknown lowercase English alphabet, return one ordering of every distinct character that satisfies the evidence, or an empty string if the evidence is inconsistent.
constraints: Each word contains only lowercase English letters

practiceProblems.name: Find Eventual Safe States
practiceProblems.statement: In a directed graph, return all vertices from which every possible path eventually ends at a terminal vertex (a vertex with no outgoing edges), in ascending order.
constraints: Each adjacency list is strictly increasing

practiceProblems.name: Parallel Courses
practiceProblems.statement: There are n courses labeled 1 through n and prerequisite edges [before, after]. In each semester any number of courses may be taken if all prerequisites were completed in earlier semesters. Return the minimum semesters to finish all courses, or -1 if a cycle makes completion impossible.

practiceProblems.name: Minimum Height Trees
practiceProblems.statement: Given an undirected tree on labels 0 through n-1, return every vertex that can be chosen as root to minimize the rooted tree height.
constraints: Input is guaranteed to be a tree
